claim: DashboardShell currently stores selectedTopicId and activeSection in React state, updates activeSection from sidebar button clicks, and uses scrollIntoView to move to section IDs rather than routing those sections through browser history.
evidence: App.tsx defines selectedTopicId/activeSection state, scrolls dashboard-section-* elements in an effect, and wires sidebar buttons to handleSectionNav.
relevance: This directly matches the user's complaint that section links scroll one giant page and should become real pages/routes.
title: Section navigation is React state plus scrolling

claim: DashboardReviewWorkflow renders overview metrics, topics list, and topic workspace in a single stacked surface; TopicWorkspace then uses local selectedTab state for Proposal, Plan, Facts, Evidence, Receipts, Health, and Graph tabs.
evidence: review-workflow.tsx defines DashboardSectionId, TopicWorkspace selectedTab state, and TabsTrigger values for the topic sections.
relevance: The page split should convert these major sections into routed pages while preserving reusable panels.
title: Topic content is one stacked workflow with local tabs

claim: MarkdownPreview resolves Cartographer reference tokens into links and currently sets the anchor title attribute to referenceTitle(reference), which delegates hover descriptions to the browser's native tooltip UI.
evidence: markdown.tsx builds cartographer-ref links, resolves references, and passes title={reference ? referenceTitle(reference) : undefined} on rendered anchors.
relevance: The requested themed popover requires replacing native title-based descriptions with a styled hover/focus component.
title: Evidence links use native title text

claim: DocumentViewer stores preview/source mode in React state, renders MarkdownPreview for preview, and renders source line anchors in a local Tabs control.
evidence: document-viewer.tsx defines mode state, TabsTrigger values for preview/source, MarkdownPreview usage, and numberedSource line anchors.
relevance: Route-owned content navigation should decide whether document modes remain local micro-state or become URL-addressable where useful.
title: Document viewer has local mode state

claim: The dashboard already uses TanStack Router/Start route files for / and /topics/$topic, and getRouter enables scrollRestoration.
evidence: routes/index.tsx and routes/topics/$topic.tsx create file routes; router.tsx creates the router with scrollRestoration: true.
relevance: The improvement should extend the existing router rather than introducing another navigation model.
title: Dashboard already has typed routes and scroll restoration

claim: TanStack Router's Link component supports typed route destinations with params and search values, including dynamic route params and search-param preservation/transforms.
evidence: Context7 TanStack Router docs show <Link to="/posts/$postId" params={{ postId }}>, Link search props, and route navigation examples.
relevance: This supports moving topic sections, document kinds, graph filters, and inspector selections into browser-history-owned routes/search params.
title: TanStack Router supports typed links with params and search state

claim: react-markdown's components option lets the renderer replace standard HTML elements such as anchors with custom React components that receive href, node, children, and props.
evidence: Context7 react-markdown docs show components={{ a({node, href, children, ...props}) { return {children} } }} and describe custom tag mappings.
relevance: The existing MarkdownPreview can replace its anchor renderer with an evidence reference link component that wraps links in a themed popover.
title: react-markdown supports custom anchor components

claim: Radix Tooltip uses aria-describedby/role=tooltip behavior and supports asChild triggers around anchors; Radix Hover Card is intended for richer hover-revealed content.
evidence: Context7 Radix primitives docs show Tooltip.Trigger asChild around anchors, TooltipContent accessibility internals, and Hover Card described as rich lightweight hover content.
relevance: The evidence hover UI can be accessible and themeable instead of relying on browser-native title tooltips.
title: Radix primitives support accessible hover/focus descriptions

claim: The local TooltipContent wrapper uses bg-popover/text-popover-foreground classes, and globals.css defines popover color tokens for both light and dark themes.
evidence: tooltip.tsx defines TooltipContent with bg-popover/text-popover-foreground; globals.css defines --popover and --popover-foreground under :root and .dark.
relevance: The hover description should feel native to the dashboard theme without inventing a separate styling system.
title: The dashboard already has themed popover primitives and tokens

claim: Mermaid's official diagram registry registers many diagram families including C4, flowchart, ER, git graph, gantt, info, pie, quadrant, xy chart, requirement, sequence, class, state, journey, timeline, mindmap, kanban, sankey, packet, radar, block, architecture, and treemap diagrams.
evidence: The official registry imports detectors for those diagram families and passes them to registerLazyLoadedDiagrams.
relevance: Dashboard Mermaid support should use the official Mermaid renderer/registry rather than a hand-written subset of diagram types.
title: Mermaid has a broad official diagram registry

claim: Mermaid can be initialized with theme/security/diagram options and can render diagram source strings asynchronously to SVG via mermaid.render.
evidence: Official examples call mermaid.initialize({...}) and await mermaid.render(id, diagramText) to obtain SVG for DOM insertion.
relevance: The dashboard Markdown renderer can add Mermaid support by detecting Mermaid code fences and invoking the official renderer with dashboard theme configuration.
title: Mermaid provides initialize and render APIs

claim: Mermaid securityLevel settings affect feature availability: strict encodes HTML tags and disables clicks, antiscript allows HTML tags except scripts and enables clicks, loose allows all HTML tags and clicks, and sandbox isolates rendering in an iframe but can limit interactivity.
evidence: Mermaid configuration docs describe strict, antiscript, loose, and sandbox security levels and note that loose is needed for click events and HTML tags in nodes.
relevance: Supporting all current Mermaid features requires an explicit design decision for secure rendering, likely via official Mermaid configuration and possibly sandbox isolation rather than silently disabling features.
title: Mermaid feature support interacts with security level
